posts.cooked:
Hello!! On our clients Online Store 2.0 theme (Dawn), a product page keeps showing the stock from before the latest order.

What happens:
Single-variant product, inventory tracked, one location, “Sell when out of stock” off. An order took 3 units. Admin then showed Available 14, Committed 0, On hand 14, and the adjustment history logs the order correctly.

The product page kept rendering variant.inventory_quantity as 17 (the value before that order) for more than 30 minutes.

Checked in a private window and with fresh requests, so it isn’t the browser cache.
Re-saving the product in admin (no real change) fixed it within a few minutes.

The Liquid is simple:

{%- assign left = product.selected_or_first_available_variant.inventory_quantity | at_least: 0 -%}
{{ left }} of {{ capacity }} left

Is this normal storefront caching? How long can a product page keep old inventory after an order?

Is there a supported way to make the page refresh after an order, without a manual save?
(Does a save from Flow or the Admin API do it, or only a save in admin?)

What’s the recommended way to show an accurate “X left” count on a Liquid theme: Storefront API quantityAvailable, or something else?

This is the store where I previously reported the issue on Safari caching problems.

All of these issues started after we built a custom event feature to showcase events as products in Shopify, without using a dedicated app.

That’s the storefront page cache, not your Liquid. Shopify caches the rendered product page, and saving the product clears it, which is why your re-save fixed it. An inventory change from an order doesn’t reliably clear it, and Shopify doesn’t document how long the old number can stay.

I wouldn’t build around forcing a save after every order through Flow or the API. It relies on cache behavior Shopify doesn’t document, and on a busy event it fires on every sale.

What I’d do for an accurate “X left”:

  1. Keep the Liquid number as the first render, so the spot is never blank.
  2. After the page loads, fetch the live number from the Storefront API: quantityAvailable on the variant. It needs the unauthenticated_read_product_inventory permission, which you can turn on for a public token in the Headless channel (or a custom app).
  3. Swap the number on the page with that result.

Also worth knowing: with “Sell when out of stock” off, checkout checks real stock, so the stale count won’t oversell your events. It only shows the wrong number.

• Capture the mismatch before re-saving the product. Confirm that Shopify Admin shows 14 available units for the same variant. In DevTools, compare the stock count in Network → Document → Response with the count shown under Elements.
  • If the HTML says 14 and the page shows 17, check whether the custom event JavaScript overwrites the count after load. Inspect any JSON or network response that supplies that value.
  • If the HTML already says 17, request the product section separately for the same variant and compare the two responses. If the section says 14, the full page and section are returning different values. If both say 17 while Admin says 14, record the timestamp, variant ID, and all three values for Shopify Support.

@LearnCurve the rendered Liquid is what gets cached, so fetch the count after load instead: call ProductVariant.quantityAvailable from the Storefront API client-side rather than printing inventory_quantity in Liquid.

ai_summary.summarized_text:
A Shopify Dawn product page continued showing 17 units for over 30 minutes after an order reduced the Admin inventory to 14. The product tracks inventory at one location, and selling when out of stock is disabled; a no-op product save eventually corrected the display. The original poster ruled out browser caching but asked whether storefront caching is expected and how to show a reliable remaining-stock count.

Replies attribute the stale value to cached rendered product-page output, which an inventory change may not reliably invalidate; Shopify’s cache duration is undocumented. They advise against saving the product after every order through Flow or the Admin API because this depends on undocumented behavior. A suggested approach is to render a Liquid fallback, then replace it after load with the variant’s Storefront API `quantityAvailable` value, requiring the appropriate inventory-read permission.

For diagnosis, compare Admin inventory with the document HTML and the displayed page, and inspect any JavaScript or network data that may overwrite the count. If Shopify responses remain stale, record the variant ID, timestamp, and values for Support. Checkout still checks actual stock, so the reported issue affects the displayed count, not overselling. No definitive platform fix or cache duration was established.
